punchline: British cycling took its riders' pillows seriously enough to pack them for races.
thirty_sec: Dave Brailsford looked for one-percent gains across British cycling. The team improved saddles, took riders' bedding to hotels, and painted its truck interior white to make dust easier to spot. James Clear tells the story in Atomic Habits. Five years after Brailsford arrived, at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, British cycling won roughly 60 percent of the cycling gold medals available.
question: What small practical change turned out to help you more than you expected?
